bottlenecks.reading: What CRDO supplies is reliable, low-power electrical connectivity over the shortest AI-rack distances (rack-scale scale-up and scale-out links of centimetres to a few metres), where the company says scale-up networks are 10x denser than scale-out and about 100x denser than front-end networks and are dominated by Ethernet and PCIe PHYs at layer 1. Paid adoption is visible in CRDO's own numbers: FY2026 revenue rose $898.3 million to $1.34 billion with over 99% of the increase from AEC shipments to hyperscalers, and the latest quarter was $479.0 million (+114.7% y/y). Management says 200G-per-lane electrical PAM4 is planned for mass deployment in 2027, so the shortage that matters is a reach / power / reliability gap at 100G and 200G per lane, not a supply gap in wafers. Management statements: read as the company's view.

CRDO's own constraint is assembly and test capacity at subcontractors, which it is paying to reserve: multiple manufacturing supply capacity reservation agreements (2 to 6 year terms) required refundable upfront deposits of $88.4 million at 2026-08-01 ($62.9 million current, $25.5 million non-current), a further agreement after the quarter commits another $102.4 million within fiscal 2027, and inventory rose $61.5 million in the quarter 'to support unfulfilled backlog and related new product ramps'. Deposits are refundable only through future purchases that meet volume requirements, so they tie CRDO's cash to the demand it expects.

A separate scarce input sits in the optical alternative: indium phosphide (InP) lasers for 200G-per-lane 1.6T optical modules. TrendForce (search excerpt, 2026-08-06) relays that Lumentum's CEO says the InP supply gap is wider than DRAM or NAND, that Lumentum was undershipping demand by about 30% in February 2026 with EML capacity committed through 2027, and that analysts expect the imbalance to persist beyond 2027; these are second-hand management claims and the page itself was not opened. This constrains optics, not CRDO's copper, and CRDO's own ZF optical transceiver line would draw on the same laser supply (see the next hypothesis).

Hypothesis: while InP lasers are short through 2027, copper (AEC) keeps its position for the shortest reaches by default, which supports CRDO's current AEC demand; the same shortage may cap how fast CRDO's ZF optical transceivers and optical DSPs can ship. No CRDO document read in this lane quantifies either effect.

Capacity and share are being added by the named competitors in the same AI-network bandwidth pool, and all four guide sharply higher: Broadcom guides AI semiconductor revenue to $21.7 billion in Q4 FY2026 (from $16.7 billion); Marvell raised its outlook, cites strong demand in Connectivity and a Custom acceleration in the second half of FY2027; Astera guides Q3 2026 revenue to $540-560 million and says Scorpio fabric switches become its largest product family one quarter early, with optical interconnect and custom solutions as expansions; Amphenol guides Q3 2026 sales to $9.3-9.4 billion with record orders (book-to-bill 1.23). The shortage is therefore being shared, not held by CRDO alone.

Hypothesis: the main threat to the copper bottleneck is optics (co-packaged or linear / retimed pluggable) taking the scale-up links as electrical reach shrinks at 224G per lane and above. Search excerpts, not registered because their dates were not seen, give vendor timelines that run from scale-up CPO revenue in 2027 (Coherent) to volume in the second half of 2027 and first customer deployments in 2028 (Lumentum), and analyst views that NVIDIA keeps copper for scale-up into 2027-2028 (SemiAnalysis) and that scale-up CPO may slip past the second half of 2028 (Bernstein, via a secondary site). The timing is unsettled and the reading is unverified until the primary reports are read. Added 2026-10-28: secondary coverage (Tom's Hardware headline, relaying SemiAnalysis; date not seen, not registered) reports NVIDIA's Kyber rack for Rubin Ultra delayed to 2028 by PCB midplane problems, with copper the only near-term option at rack scale; Marvell management at its 2026-10-06 Investor Day said 100% of XPU-to-XPU links run on copper today, copper reach at 200G per lane is 2.5 metres, and scale-up optics are at virtually zero revenue with multi-hundred-million-dollar revenue starting next year (fd_ind_futurum_mrvl_20261009). Both point to copper holding scale-up into 2027-2028 and optics starting to take links from 2027; still unverified at the primary level.

An attributed analyst estimate (Jefferies, reported by Invezz 2026-04-13, search excerpt, page not opened) puts the AEC market at 8.6 million units in 2026 and 12.3 million in 2027 and calls CRDO 'the outright technology leader' with pressure from Astera and Marvell. This is a third-party expectation, not a reported fact.

A named competitor's management confirms the copper position CRDO sells into: at Marvell's 2026-10-06 Investor Day (reported by Futurum 2026-10-09) management said 100% of XPU-to-XPU links run on copper today, that copper reach at 200G per lane is 2.5 metres, and that scale-up optics run at virtually zero revenue today with multi-hundred-million-dollar revenue starting next year. This is a competitor's view relayed by an industry analyst, not a CRDO number; it supports the reach-gap reading and dates the optical challenge to about 2027.

The AEC position is being contested at 1.6T: MaxLinear's CEO (Q3 2026 call of 2026-10-22, reported by Stocktwits 2026-10-23) put CRDO at an estimated 93-99% of the AEC market and set a target of 20-30% of the 1.6T AEC market over the next couple of years, supplying silicon to cable makers; MaxLinear's own release reports infrastructure revenue +210% y/y to $124.9M on its Keystone PAM4 DSP ramp and names its 1.6T-capable Rushmore and Annapurna families. CRDO's own call (2026-09-01) placed 1.6T AEC at some contribution in H2 FY2027 and a meaningful ramp in FY2028, so the entrant aims at the generation CRDO is about to ramp. CRDO fell about 10% intraday on 2026-10-23 on the report. The share figure is a competitor CEO's estimate and the target is an ambition, not a reported outcome.
